cards.text: Jesus and the people traveling with Him are on the road again, and He comes into a village. Somebody there is about to welcome Him in. Friend, the best trip I ever took started in the back of a junk drawer, and I didn't even get to pack.

cards.question: In this village, a woman named Martha welcomes Jesus into her ___.

cards.text: Martha has a sister named Mary. Now keep your eye on Mary, friend, because she's about to find her spot with Jesus in the house.

cards.question: Martha's sister Mary finds a spot near Jesus. What does she do there?

answers.text: Sits at His feet listening to Him
Brings Him a bowl of fresh water
Asks Him to bless the whole house

cards.text: But Martha is distracted by all the preparations to be made. I KNOW that look, friend. That's me with four timers going off at once and my apron on backwards.

cards.question: Martha comes to Jesus and asks if He doesn't care about something. What is it?

answers.text: That her sister left her to serve alone
That the house is too small for everyone
That His followers came without warning

cards.question: True or false: Martha asks Jesus to tell Mary to help her.

cards.text: "Martha, Martha," the Lord replies. When somebody says your name TWICE, you put down whatever you're holding. Spoon, dish towel, everything. Down.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus tells Martha she is worried and upset about many things.

cards.text: Then Jesus tells Martha what's necessary. Friend, I'm leaning in so far on this one, my gold base is about to tip over.

cards.question: Jesus tells Martha that only ___ thing is necessary.
Jesus says Mary has chosen the good portion. What does He say about it?

answers.text: It will not be taken away from her
She has to set it aside for now
She can have it once the work is done

cards.question: True or false: Jesus sends Mary off to help Martha with the preparations.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the sentence about Martha's distraction, followed by two separate joke sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card is punctuated as four sentences, including the separate fragments about the spoon and dish towel and the final 'Down.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The singular word 'thing' makes 'one' the only grammatically possible completion. Choosing 'two' or 'three' would produce 'two thing' or 'three thing,' so the wrong answers are not believable and the correct answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
